title: Webinar scheduling across time zones
scenario: A 10:00 IST webinar showed as 10:00 for attendees in London, and daylight saving moved US sessions by an hour.
stack: Spring Boot 4.1.1 · Java 25 · java.time (Instant, LocalDateTime, ZonedDateTime, ZoneRules, TemporalAdjusters) · Clock with @TestBean · RFC 9457 problem details
simulation: Webinars are demo records kept in memory: no video room, invitation or reminder is created, and they are gone when the app restarts. Time zone rules are the ones shipped with the JDK that ran the captures.

  • What this station is not

Level 1, about 5 minutes. Plain language: no code.

The problem in real life

  1. 10:00 for everyone

    Taskloom's host in Bengaluru set a webinar for 10:00. Attendees in London saw 10:00 too, and joined five and a half hours late.

  2. Then an hour off

    A fix stored the moment in UTC, but repeated series by adding a month in UTC. When the US left daylight saving, a New York host's 10:00 sessions moved to 09:00.

  3. The fix

    Turn the host's wall-clock time into a moment using the host's zone, separately for every session; store the moment; show it in each viewer's zone.

A clock time without a place is not a moment. Store the moment; show it in each person's own clock.

What are we building?

A host creates a webinar at their own wall-clock time and zone (POST /webinars), optionally repeating monthly. Anyone reads it in their zone (GET /webinars/{id}?viewerZone=…), and every session shows the moment in UTC, the host's time and the viewer's time, each with its offset.

An everyday analogy

A train timetable says 10:00 because everyone reading it is at that station. A video call has no single station: you send "10:00 in Bengaluru", and each person's phone turns it into their own time. The phone needs the place, not just "10:00".

How it works in 4 steps

  1. The host sends 10:00, 5 Nov, Asia/Kolkata.
  2. The server asks the zone's rules which offset that wall time has on that date (+05:30), refusing a time that is skipped or repeated.
  3. It stores the moment, 04:30 UTC, with the host's zone.
  4. Each viewer sees that moment in their own zone: 04:30 in London, 20:30 the evening before in Los Angeles.
Check yourself: a monthly New York webinar at 10:00. Why does it move from 19:30 to 20:30 in India in November?

New York leaves daylight saving on 1 November (−04:00 becomes −05:00); India has no daylight saving. The host's 10:00 stays 10:00, so the moment moves one hour later, and India sees it an hour later. That is correct. The old code kept the moment fixed and moved the host.

What this station is not

  • No reminders or invitations. Times only.
  • No weekly series. Challenge 1.
  • No database. Webinars live in memory.

Key terms

TermSimple meaningEveryday exampleIn this project
InstantOne moment on the world's timeline, the same everywhere.The moment a cricket match's first ball is bowled.startsAt (UTC)
LocalDateTimeA date and a clock time, with no place: it is not a moment."10:00 on 5 Nov" written on a sticky note.What the host types
Time zoneA region's rules for its clocks, including daylight saving.Asia/Kolkata, Europe/London.zone, viewerZone
OffsetHow far a clock is from UTC at one moment.India is always +05:30; London is +00:00 or +01:00.+05:30 in each time shown
Daylight saving gap / overlapAn hour that does not exist, or happens twice, when clocks jump.02:30 on the night US clocks spring forward.422 answers
ClockWhere the program asks "what time is it now?".The office wall clock everyone checks.A fixed Clock in tests

  • 1. Business problem
  • 2. Acceptance criteria

Level 2. What a teammate hands you before you build.

Business problem

Taskloom (a fictional SaaS for project teams) runs webinars for customers in many countries. Times were shown wrongly abroad and drifted when daylight saving changed.

Acceptance criteria

  1. Given 10:00 on 5 Nov 2026 in Asia/Kolkata, then London sees 04:30 and Los Angeles 20:30 on 4 Nov.
  2. Given a monthly 10:00 series in New York from 20 Oct, then the host sees 10:00 both months, and India sees 19:30, then 20:30.
  3. Given monthly from 31 Jan 2027, then 28 Feb, 31 Mar, 30 Apr; from 31 Jan 2028, 29 Feb.
  4. Given a time the clocks skip (02:30, 14 Mar 2027, New York), then 422; a time that happens twice (01:30, 1 Nov 2026), 422 unless the offset is named.
  5. Given a first session that has already started by the server's clock, then 422.
  6. Given IST or +05:30 as a zone, a malformed date, or 10 minutes, then 400; an unknown webinar, 404.

Requirements

  • Store moments (Instant) and the host's zone; never a bare LocalDateTime.
  • Each session of a series is resolved on its own date in the host's zone.
  • Zones are region ids (Asia/Kolkata), never abbreviations or fixed offsets.
  • "Now" comes from an injected Clock.

Learning objectives

  • Tell Instant, LocalDateTime, ZonedDateTime and OffsetDateTime apart and pick the right one.
  • Handle daylight saving gaps and overlaps on purpose.
  • Do date arithmetic in the right zone, and with month ends and leap years.
  • Test time-dependent code with a fixed Clock.

  • 5. API contract

Examples are captured with curl from the running app, never typed by hand.

Endpoints

MethodPathPurpose
POST/webinarsCreate: title, startsAt (host's wall-clock time, no offset), zone, durationMinutes (15 to 480), optional repeat (NONE, MONTHLY, MONTHLY_LAST_WEEKDAY) and sessions (1 to 12), optional offset for a time that happens twice.
GET/webinars/{id}?viewerZone=Europe/LondonEvery session as startsAt (UTC), hostTime and viewerTime. Without viewerZone, the host's zone.

Status codes

StatusWhen
201Created; Location points at it
200The webinar, in the viewer's zone
400Malformed body, an unknown zone (including IST and +05:30), duration or sessions out of range
404No such webinar
422Already started; a time skipped or repeated by daylight saving; a series that does not fit its rule

Every edge case points at the test that proves it.

Edge cases

CaseWhat happensProved by
Created in India, viewed in Los AngelesThe evening before, 20:30createdInTheHostZoneAndShownInAnyOther
Starts this minute, or the next422, then 201 (fixed Clock)theFirstMinuteThatCountsIsTheClocks
A skipped time, US and UK422aTimeTheClocksSkipIsRefused
A repeated time, with and without offset422; 201 with the right offset; 422 with a wrong oneaTimeThatHappensTwiceNeedsAnOffset
Monthly from the 31st; leap yearMonth ends kept; 29 Feb 2028monthlyFromThe31stKeepsToTheMonthEnd
Last Friday of each month30 Oct, 27 Nov, 25 Dec; a date that is not the last Friday is 422lastFridayOfEachMonth
IST, +05:30, a non-ISO date, 10 minutes, 13 sessions, unknown repeat, bad viewer zone400brokenRequestsAre400
Unknown webinar404unknownWebinarsAre404

The trap

Plausible but wrong

Storing LocalDateTime without a zone, so times shift for other countries.

The old code is kept in the tests as OldWebinarStore, in both versions. The first stored LocalDateTime: asked for London, it can only answer 10:00, because the zone was never kept. The second stored an Instant but added months in UTC: a New York session at 10:00 on 20 October came back at 09:00 on 20 November, after the US left daylight saving. The fixed API runs the same two webinars and gets 04:30 for London, and 10:00 for the New York host in both months.

While building, each part was undone once. Adding 30 days instead of a month turned 2 tests red; dropping the "happens twice" check, 1; showing the host's time to the viewer, 3; repeating in UTC, 2; asking Instant.now() instead of the Clock, 1 (the fixed-clock test); accepting offsets and abbreviations as zones, 1.

package com.taskloom.webinars;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import java.time.Instant;
import java.time.LocalDateTime;
import java.time.ZoneId;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.request.MockMvcRequestBuilders.get;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.MockMvcResultMatchers.jsonPath;

/** The first test written for this station: both bugs from the support tickets, then the same webinars through the fixed API. */
class LocalDateTimeTrapTest extends ApiTest {

    @Test
    void aLocalDateTimeShowsTenOClockToEveryone() throws Exception {
        var old = new OldWebinarStore.OldWebinar("Planning your first sprint", LocalDateTime.parse("2026-11-05T10:00"));
        assertThat(old.showTo("Europe/London")).isEqualTo(LocalDateTime.parse("2026-11-05T10:00"));   // 10:00 in London: wrong by 5h30

        String url = created(webinar("2026-11-05T10:00", "Asia/Kolkata", ""));
        mvc.perform(get(url).param("viewerZone", "Europe/London"))
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.sessions[0].startsAt").value("2026-11-05T04:30:00Z"))
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.sessions[0].hostTime").value("2026-11-05T10:00:00+05:30"))
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.sessions[0].viewerTime").value("2026-11-05T04:30:00Z"));
    }

    @Test
    void repeatingInUtcMovesANewYorkSessionWhenDaylightSavingEnds() throws Exception {
        // 10:00 in New York on 20 Oct is 14:00 UTC. The US leaves daylight saving on 1 Nov 2026.
        var old = OldWebinarStore.monthlyInUtc(Instant.parse("2026-10-20T14:00:00Z"), 2);
        assertThat(old.get(1).atZone(ZoneId.of("America/New_York")).toLocalTime()).hasToString("09:00");   // the host's 10:00 became 09:00

        String url = created(webinar("2026-10-20T10:00", "America/New_York", ",\"repeat\":\"MONTHLY\",\"sessions\":2"));
        mvc.perform(get(url).param("viewerZone", "Asia/Kolkata"))
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.sessions[1].hostTime").value("2026-11-20T10:00:00-05:00"))     // still 10:00 for the host
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.sessions[0].viewerTime").value("2026-10-20T19:30:00+05:30"))
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.sessions[1].viewerTime").value("2026-11-20T20:30:00+05:30"));  // an hour later in India, correctly
    }
}
package com.taskloom.webinars;

import java.time.Instant;
import java.time.LocalDateTime;
import java.time.ZoneOffset;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.stream.IntStream;

/** The scheduling code as it shipped, kept only in tests. */
class OldWebinarStore {

    /** Stored a LocalDateTime: 10:00, with no idea where. Every viewer got the same 10:00. */
    record OldWebinar(String title, LocalDateTime startsAt) {
        LocalDateTime showTo(String viewerZone) {
            return startsAt;   // nothing to convert from: the zone was never kept
        }
    }

    /** The later version stored an Instant, but repeated it by adding months in UTC, not in the host's zone. */
    static List<Instant> monthlyInUtc(Instant first, int count) {
        return IntStream.range(0, count).mapToObj(i -> first.atZone(ZoneOffset.UTC).plusMonths(i).toInstant()).toList();
    }
}

In the order a request travels.

src/main/java/com/taskloom/webinars/WebinarController.java

Does

Why
Zones checked at the edge, with a reason.
Without it

package com.taskloom.webinars;

import jakarta.validation.Valid;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Max;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Min;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.NotNull;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Size;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail;
import org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity;
import org.springframework.web.ErrorResponseException;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PathVariable;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PostMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestBody;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestParam;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

import java.net.URI;
import java.time.LocalDateTime;
import java.time.ZoneId;
import java.time.ZoneOffset;

@RestController
class WebinarController {

    /**
     * startsAt is the host's wall-clock time, with no offset; zone says where that wall is. The offset is only for
     * the one hour a year when the host's clock shows the same time twice.
     */
    record NewWebinar(@NotBlank @Size(max = 120) String title, @NotNull LocalDateTime startsAt, @NotBlank String zone,
                      @NotNull @Min(15) @Max(480) Integer durationMinutes, Schedule.Repeat repeat,
                      @Min(1) @Max(12) Integer sessions, ZoneOffset offset) {
    }

    private final Schedule schedule;

    WebinarController(Schedule schedule) {
        this.schedule = schedule;
    }

    @PostMapping("/webinars")
    ResponseEntity<Schedule.WebinarView> create(@Valid @RequestBody NewWebinar body) {
        Schedule.WebinarView webinar = schedule.create(body.title().strip(), body.startsAt(), region(body.zone(), "zone"), body.offset(),
                body.durationMinutes(), body.repeat() == null ? Schedule.Repeat.NONE : body.repeat(), body.sessions() == null ? 1 : body.sessions());
        return ResponseEntity.created(URI.create("/webinars/" + webinar.id())).body(webinar);
    }

    @GetMapping("/webinars/{id}")
    Schedule.WebinarView get(@PathVariable long id, @RequestParam(required = false) String viewerZone) {
        return schedule.find(id, viewerZone == null ? null : region(viewerZone, "viewerZone"))
                .orElseThrow(() -> problem(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "Webinar not found", "No webinar " + id + "."));
    }

    /**
     * Only region ids such as Asia/Kolkata (and UTC). A fixed offset like +05:30 knows nothing about daylight saving,
     * and abbreviations like IST are ambiguous (India, Ireland, Israel).
     */
    static ZoneId region(String id, String field) {
        if (!ZoneId.getAvailableZoneIds().contains(id)) {
            throw problem(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "Unknown time zone", field + " must be a time zone region such as Asia/Kolkata or Europe/London, not \"" + id + "\".");
        }
        return ZoneId.of(id);
    }

    static ErrorResponseException problem(HttpStatus status, String title, String detail) {
        ProblemDetail p = ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(status, detail);
        p.setTitle(title);
        return new ErrorResponseException(status, p, null);
    }
}

src/main/java/com/taskloom/webinars/Schedule.java

Does
Turns each session's wall-clock time into a moment in the host's zone, and moments into anyone's time.
Why
One place knows about gaps, overlaps, month ends and the Clock.
Without it
Times that shift abroad or at daylight saving.
  • getValidOffsets returns 0 offsets in a gap and 2 in an overlap; both are refused unless the client chose.
  • Monthly sessions are startsAt.plusMonths(i) from the first date, never chained: 31 Jan → 28 Feb → 31 Mar.
  • TemporalAdjusters.lastInMonth finds the last Friday.
package com.taskloom.webinars;

import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import org.springframework.web.ErrorResponseException;

import java.time.Clock;
import java.time.DayOfWeek;
import java.time.Instant;
import java.time.LocalDateTime;
import java.time.OffsetDateTime;
import java.time.ZoneId;
import java.time.ZoneOffset;
import java.time.temporal.TemporalAdjusters;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Optional;
import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicLong;

/**
 * Turns the host's wall-clock time into instants (UTC) when a webinar is created, and instants back into anyone's
 * wall-clock time when it is read. Every session of a series is resolved on its own date, in the host's zone.
 */
@Service
class Schedule {

    enum Repeat { NONE, MONTHLY, MONTHLY_LAST_WEEKDAY }

    /** What is kept: the host's zone and the instants. No LocalDateTime is stored, because it means nothing alone. */
    record Webinar(long id, String title, ZoneId hostZone, int durationMinutes, List<Instant> sessions) {
    }

    record Session(Instant startsAt, OffsetDateTime hostTime, OffsetDateTime viewerTime) {
    }

    record WebinarView(long id, String title, String hostZone, String viewerZone, int durationMinutes, List<Session> sessions) {
    }

    private final Clock clock;
    private final Map<Long, Webinar> webinars = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();   // shortcut: in memory, lost on restart; a real app uses a table
    private final AtomicLong ids = new AtomicLong();

    Schedule(Clock clock) {
        this.clock = clock;
    }

    WebinarView create(String title, LocalDateTime startsAt, ZoneId zone, ZoneOffset offset, int durationMinutes, Repeat repeat, int count) {
        if (repeat == Repeat.NONE && count != 1) {
            throw unprocessable("A one-off webinar has 1 session; use repeat MONTHLY or MONTHLY_LAST_WEEKDAY for " + count + ".");
        }
        DayOfWeek weekday = startsAt.getDayOfWeek();
        if (repeat == Repeat.MONTHLY_LAST_WEEKDAY && !startsAt.toLocalDate().equals(startsAt.toLocalDate().with(TemporalAdjusters.lastInMonth(weekday)))) {
            throw unprocessable(startsAt.toLocalDate() + " is not the last " + weekday + " of its month.");
        }
        List<Instant> sessions = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
            LocalDateTime local = switch (repeat) {
                // Always from the first date: Jan 31 + 1 month = Feb 28 (or 29), + 2 months = Mar 31. Chaining would stick at 28.
                case NONE, MONTHLY -> startsAt.plusMonths(i);
                case MONTHLY_LAST_WEEKDAY -> startsAt.plusMonths(i).with(TemporalAdjusters.lastInMonth(weekday));
            };
            sessions.add(resolve(local, zone, i == 0 ? offset : null));
        }
        if (!sessions.getFirst().isAfter(clock.instant())) {
            throw unprocessable("The first session, " + startsAt + " in " + zone + ", has already started.");
        }
        Webinar webinar = new Webinar(ids.incrementAndGet(), title, zone, durationMinutes, List.copyOf(sessions));
        webinars.put(webinar.id(), webinar);
        return view(webinar, zone);
    }

    Optional<WebinarView> find(long id, ZoneId viewerZone) {
        return Optional.ofNullable(webinars.get(id)).map(w -> view(w, viewerZone == null ? w.hostZone() : viewerZone));
    }

    /**
     * A wall-clock time in a zone is not always one instant: in a daylight saving gap it is none (clocks jump past
     * it), in an overlap it is two (clocks repeat it). Both are refused unless the client names the offset it means.
     */
    static Instant resolve(LocalDateTime local, ZoneId zone, ZoneOffset offset) {
        List<ZoneOffset> valid = zone.getRules().getValidOffsets(local);
        if (valid.isEmpty()) {
            throw unprocessable(local + " does not exist in " + zone + ": the clocks skip it for daylight saving.");
        }
        if (offset != null) {
            if (!valid.contains(offset)) {
                throw unprocessable(local + " in " + zone + " is at " + valid.getFirst() + ", not " + offset + ".");
            }
            return local.atOffset(offset).toInstant();
        }
        if (valid.size() > 1) {
            throw unprocessable(local + " happens twice in " + zone + " (" + valid.get(0) + " and " + valid.get(1)
                    + ") as the clocks go back; send \"offset\" to choose.");
        }
        return local.atOffset(valid.getFirst()).toInstant();
    }

    private static WebinarView view(Webinar w, ZoneId viewer) {
        List<Session> sessions = w.sessions().stream()
                .map(s -> new Session(s, s.atZone(w.hostZone()).toOffsetDateTime(), s.atZone(viewer).toOffsetDateTime())).toList();
        return new WebinarView(w.id(), w.title(), w.hostZone().getId(), viewer.getId(), w.durationMinutes(), sessions);
    }

    static ErrorResponseException unprocessable(String detail) {
        ProblemDetail p = ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, detail);
        p.setTitle("Not a schedulable time");
        return new ErrorResponseException(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, p, null);
    }
}

package com.taskloom.webinars;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import java.time.Instant;
import java.time.LocalDateTime;
import java.time.ZoneId;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.request.MockMvcRequestBuilders.get;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.MockMvcResultMatchers.jsonPath;

/** The first test written for this station: both bugs from the support tickets, then the same webinars through the fixed API. */
class LocalDateTimeTrapTest extends ApiTest {

    @Test
    void aLocalDateTimeShowsTenOClockToEveryone() throws Exception {
        var old = new OldWebinarStore.OldWebinar("Planning your first sprint", LocalDateTime.parse("2026-11-05T10:00"));
        assertThat(old.showTo("Europe/London")).isEqualTo(LocalDateTime.parse("2026-11-05T10:00"));   // 10:00 in London: wrong by 5h30

        String url = created(webinar("2026-11-05T10:00", "Asia/Kolkata", ""));
        mvc.perform(get(url).param("viewerZone", "Europe/London"))
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.sessions[0].startsAt").value("2026-11-05T04:30:00Z"))
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.sessions[0].hostTime").value("2026-11-05T10:00:00+05:30"))
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.sessions[0].viewerTime").value("2026-11-05T04:30:00Z"));
    }

    @Test
    void repeatingInUtcMovesANewYorkSessionWhenDaylightSavingEnds() throws Exception {
        // 10:00 in New York on 20 Oct is 14:00 UTC. The US leaves daylight saving on 1 Nov 2026.
        var old = OldWebinarStore.monthlyInUtc(Instant.parse("2026-10-20T14:00:00Z"), 2);
        assertThat(old.get(1).atZone(ZoneId.of("America/New_York")).toLocalTime()).hasToString("09:00");   // the host's 10:00 became 09:00

        String url = created(webinar("2026-10-20T10:00", "America/New_York", ",\"repeat\":\"MONTHLY\",\"sessions\":2"));
        mvc.perform(get(url).param("viewerZone", "Asia/Kolkata"))
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.sessions[1].hostTime").value("2026-11-20T10:00:00-05:00"))     // still 10:00 for the host
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.sessions[0].viewerTime").value("2026-10-20T19:30:00+05:30"))
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.sessions[1].viewerTime").value("2026-11-20T20:30:00+05:30"));  // an hour later in India, correctly
    }
}

package com.taskloom.webinars;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import static org.hamcrest.Matchers.contains;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.request.MockMvcRequestBuilders.get;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.MockMvcResultMatchers.header;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.MockMvcResultMatchers.jsonPath;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.MockMvcResultMatchers.status;

/** The HTTP contract: create and view in any zone; daylight saving, month ends; 400, 422 and 404. */
class WebinarContractTest extends ApiTest {

    @Test
    void createdInTheHostZoneAndShownInAnyOther() throws Exception {
        String url = create(webinar("2026-11-05T10:00", "Asia/Kolkata", "")).andExpect(status().isCreated())
                .andExpect(header().string("Location", org.hamcrest.Matchers.matchesPattern("/webinars/[0-9]+")))
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.viewerZone").value("Asia/Kolkata")).andExpect(jsonPath("$.sessions[0].viewerTime").value("2026-11-05T10:00:00+05:30"))
                .andReturn().getResponse().getHeader("Location");
        mvc.perform(get(url).param("viewerZone", "America/Los_Angeles"))
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.sessions[0].viewerTime").value("2026-11-04T20:30:00-08:00"));   // the evening before
        mvc.perform(get(url)).andExpect(jsonPath("$.viewerZone").value("Asia/Kolkata"));
    }

    @Test
    void theFirstMinuteThatCountsIsTheClocks() throws Exception {
        // Now is 11:30 in India. 11:30 has started; 11:31 has not.
        create(webinar("2026-10-16T11:30", "Asia/Kolkata", "")).andExpect(status().isUnprocessableContent());
        create(webinar("2026-10-16T11:31", "Asia/Kolkata", "")).andExpect(status().isCreated());
    }

    @Test
    void aTimeTheClocksSkipIsRefused() throws Exception {
        create(webinar("2027-03-14T02:30", "America/New_York", "")).andExpect(status().isUnprocessableContent())
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.detail").value("2027-03-14T02:30 does not exist in America/New_York: the clocks skip it for daylight saving."));
        create(webinar("2027-03-28T01:30", "Europe/London", "")).andExpect(status().isUnprocessableContent());
    }

    @Test
    void aTimeThatHappensTwiceNeedsAnOffset() throws Exception {
        create(webinar("2026-11-01T01:30", "America/New_York", "")).andExpect(status().isUnprocessableContent())
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.detail").value(org.hamcrest.Matchers.containsString("-04:00 and -05:00")));
        create(webinar("2026-11-01T01:30", "America/New_York", ",\"offset\":\"-05:00\"")).andExpect(status().isCreated())
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.sessions[0].startsAt").value("2026-11-01T06:30:00Z"));
        create(webinar("2026-11-01T01:30", "America/New_York", ",\"offset\":\"+05:30\"")).andExpect(status().isUnprocessableContent());
    }

    @Test
    void monthlyFromThe31stKeepsToTheMonthEnd() throws Exception {
        create(webinar("2027-01-31T10:00", "Asia/Kolkata", ",\"repeat\":\"MONTHLY\",\"sessions\":4")).andExpect(status().isCreated())
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.sessions[*].hostTime", contains("2027-01-31T10:00:00+05:30", "2027-02-28T10:00:00+05:30",
                        "2027-03-31T10:00:00+05:30", "2027-04-30T10:00:00+05:30")));
        create(webinar("2028-01-31T10:00", "Asia/Kolkata", ",\"repeat\":\"MONTHLY\",\"sessions\":2"))
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.sessions[1].hostTime").value("2028-02-29T10:00:00+05:30"));   // a leap year
    }

    @Test
    void lastFridayOfEachMonth() throws Exception {
        create(webinar("2026-10-30T16:00", "Asia/Kolkata", ",\"repeat\":\"MONTHLY_LAST_WEEKDAY\",\"sessions\":3")).andExpect(status().isCreated())
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.sessions[*].hostTime", contains("2026-10-30T16:00:00+05:30", "2026-11-27T16:00:00+05:30", "2026-12-25T16:00:00+05:30")));
        create(webinar("2026-10-23T16:00", "Asia/Kolkata", ",\"repeat\":\"MONTHLY_LAST_WEEKDAY\",\"sessions\":3"))
                .andExpect(status().isUnprocessableContent()).andExpect(jsonPath("$.detail").value("2026-10-23 is not the last FRIDAY of its month."));
    }

    @Test
    void brokenRequestsAre400() throws Exception {
        create(webinar("2026-11-05T10:00", "IST", "")).andExpect(status().isBadRequest()).andExpect(jsonPath("$.title").value("Unknown time zone"));
        create(webinar("2026-11-05T10:00", "+05:30", "")).andExpect(status().isBadRequest());
        create(webinar("05/11/2026 10:00", "Asia/Kolkata", "")).andExpect(status().isBadRequest());
        create(webinar("2026-11-05T10:00", "Asia/Kolkata", "").replace("60", "10")).andExpect(status().isBadRequest());   // under 15 minutes
        create(webinar("2026-11-05T10:00", "Asia/Kolkata", ",\"sessions\":13")).andExpect(status().isBadRequest());
        create(webinar("2026-11-05T10:00", "Asia/Kolkata", ",\"repeat\":\"DAILY\"")).andExpect(status().isBadRequest());
        create(webinar("2026-11-05T10:00", "Asia/Kolkata", ",\"sessions\":3")).andExpect(status().isUnprocessableContent());   // one-off with 3 sessions
        String url = created(webinar("2026-11-05T10:00", "Asia/Kolkata", ""));
        mvc.perform(get(url).param("viewerZone", "Mars/Olympus")).andExpect(status().isBadRequest());
    }

    @Test
    void unknownWebinarsAre404() throws Exception {
        mvc.perform(get("/webinars/999999")).andExpect(status().isNotFound()).andExpect(jsonPath("$.detail").value("No webinar 999999."));
    }
}

package com.taskloom.webinars;

import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;
import org.springframework.boot.webmvc.test.autoconfigure.AutoConfigureMockMvc;
import org.springframework.http.MediaType;
import org.springframework.test.context.bean.override.convention.TestBean;
import org.springframework.test.web.servlet.MockMvc;
import org.springframework.test.web.servlet.ResultActions;

import java.time.Clock;
import java.time.Instant;
import java.time.ZoneOffset;

import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.request.MockMvcRequestBuilders.post;

/**
 * Shared setup: the whole app with its Clock replaced by a fixed one. "Now" is 16 Oct 2026, 06:00 UTC (11:30 in
 * India), in every test, on every machine, in every month of the year.
 */
@SpringBootTest
@AutoConfigureMockMvc
abstract class ApiTest {

    static final Instant NOW = Instant.parse("2026-10-16T06:00:00Z");

    @TestBean
    Clock clock;

    static Clock clock() {
        return Clock.fixed(NOW, ZoneOffset.UTC);
    }

    @Autowired
    MockMvc mvc;

    /** A 60-minute webinar; extra is appended inside the JSON object, e.g. ",\"repeat\":\"MONTHLY\"". */
    static String webinar(String startsAt, String zone, String extra) {
        return "{\"title\":\"Planning your first sprint\",\"startsAt\":\"%s\",\"zone\":\"%s\",\"durationMinutes\":60%s}".formatted(startsAt, zone, extra);
    }

    ResultActions create(String body) throws Exception {
        return mvc.perform(post("/webinars").contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON).content(body));
    }

    /** Creates the webinar and returns its URL (the store is shared by every test, so ids are not predictable). */
    String created(String body) throws Exception {
        return create(body).andReturn().getResponse().getHeader("Location");
    }
}

package com.taskloom.webinars;

import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import org.springframework.web.ErrorResponseException;

import java.time.Clock;
import java.time.DayOfWeek;
import java.time.Duration;
import java.time.Instant;
import java.time.LocalDateTime;
import java.time.OffsetDateTime;
import java.time.ZoneId;
import java.time.ZoneOffset;
import java.time.temporal.ChronoUnit;
import java.time.temporal.TemporalAdjusters;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Optional;
import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicLong;

/**
 * Turns the host's wall-clock time into instants (UTC) when a webinar is created, and instants back into anyone's
 * wall-clock time when it is read. Every session of a series is resolved on its own date, in the host's zone.
 */
@Service
class Schedule {

    enum Repeat { NONE, WEEKLY, MONTHLY, MONTHLY_LAST_WEEKDAY }

    /** What is kept: the host's zone and the instants. No LocalDateTime is stored, because it means nothing alone. */
    record Webinar(long id, String title, ZoneId hostZone, int durationMinutes, List<Instant> sessions) {
    }

    record Session(Instant startsAt, OffsetDateTime hostTime, OffsetDateTime viewerTime, OffsetDateTime viewerEndTime, long viewerDayShift) {
    }

    record WebinarView(long id, String title, String hostZone, String viewerZone, int durationMinutes, List<Session> sessions) {
    }

    private final Clock clock;
    private final Map<Long, Webinar> webinars = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();   // shortcut: in memory, lost on restart; a real app uses a table
    private final AtomicLong ids = new AtomicLong();

    Schedule(Clock clock) {
        this.clock = clock;
    }

    WebinarView create(String title, LocalDateTime startsAt, ZoneId zone, ZoneOffset offset, int durationMinutes, Repeat repeat, int count) {
        if (repeat == Repeat.NONE && count != 1) {
            throw unprocessable("A one-off webinar has 1 session; use repeat MONTHLY or MONTHLY_LAST_WEEKDAY for " + count + ".");
        }
        DayOfWeek weekday = startsAt.getDayOfWeek();
        if (repeat == Repeat.MONTHLY_LAST_WEEKDAY && !startsAt.toLocalDate().equals(startsAt.toLocalDate().with(TemporalAdjusters.lastInMonth(weekday)))) {
            throw unprocessable(startsAt.toLocalDate() + " is not the last " + weekday + " of its month.");
        }
        List<Instant> sessions = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
            LocalDateTime local = switch (repeat) {
                // Always from the first date: Jan 31 + 1 month = Feb 28 (or 29), + 2 months = Mar 31. Chaining would stick at 28.
                case WEEKLY -> startsAt.plusWeeks(i);   // wall-clock weeks in the host's zone, not 7 x 24 hours
                case NONE, MONTHLY -> startsAt.plusMonths(i);
                case MONTHLY_LAST_WEEKDAY -> startsAt.plusMonths(i).with(TemporalAdjusters.lastInMonth(weekday));
            };
            sessions.add(resolve(local, zone, i == 0 ? offset : null));
        }
        if (!sessions.getFirst().isAfter(clock.instant())) {
            throw unprocessable("The first session, " + startsAt + " in " + zone + ", has already started.");
        }
        Webinar webinar = new Webinar(ids.incrementAndGet(), title, zone, durationMinutes, List.copyOf(sessions));
        webinars.put(webinar.id(), webinar);
        return view(webinar, zone);
    }

    Optional<WebinarView> find(long id, ZoneId viewerZone) {
        return Optional.ofNullable(webinars.get(id)).map(w -> view(w, viewerZone == null ? w.hostZone() : viewerZone));
    }

    /**
     * A wall-clock time in a zone is not always one instant: in a daylight saving gap it is none (clocks jump past
     * it), in an overlap it is two (clocks repeat it). Both are refused unless the client names the offset it means.
     */
    static Instant resolve(LocalDateTime local, ZoneId zone, ZoneOffset offset) {
        List<ZoneOffset> valid = zone.getRules().getValidOffsets(local);
        if (valid.isEmpty()) {
            throw unprocessable(local + " does not exist in " + zone + ": the clocks skip it for daylight saving.");
        }
        if (offset != null) {
            if (!valid.contains(offset)) {
                throw unprocessable(local + " in " + zone + " is at " + valid.getFirst() + ", not " + offset + ".");
            }
            return local.atOffset(offset).toInstant();
        }
        if (valid.size() > 1) {
            throw unprocessable(local + " happens twice in " + zone + " (" + valid.get(0) + " and " + valid.get(1)
                    + ") as the clocks go back; send \"offset\" to choose.");
        }
        return local.atOffset(valid.getFirst()).toInstant();
    }

    private static WebinarView view(Webinar w, ZoneId viewer) {
        List<Session> sessions = w.sessions().stream()
                .map(s -> new Session(s, s.atZone(w.hostZone()).toOffsetDateTime(), s.atZone(viewer).toOffsetDateTime(),
                        s.plus(Duration.ofMinutes(w.durationMinutes())).atZone(viewer).toOffsetDateTime(),
                        ChronoUnit.DAYS.between(s.atZone(w.hostZone()).toLocalDate(), s.atZone(viewer).toLocalDate()))).toList();
        return new WebinarView(w.id(), w.title(), w.hostZone().getId(), viewer.getId(), w.durationMinutes(), sessions);
    }

    static ErrorResponseException unprocessable(String detail) {
        ProblemDetail p = ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, detail);
        p.setTitle("Not a schedulable time");
        return new ErrorResponseException(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, p, null);
    }
}

challenge/solution/Schedule.java

package com.taskloom.webinars;

import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import org.springframework.web.ErrorResponseException;

import java.time.Clock;
import java.time.DayOfWeek;
import java.time.Duration;
import java.time.Instant;
import java.time.LocalDateTime;
import java.time.OffsetDateTime;
import java.time.ZoneId;
import java.time.ZoneOffset;
import java.time.temporal.ChronoUnit;
import java.time.temporal.TemporalAdjusters;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Optional;
import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicLong;

/**
 * Turns the host's wall-clock time into instants (UTC) when a webinar is created, and instants back into anyone's
 * wall-clock time when it is read. Every session of a series is resolved on its own date, in the host's zone.
 */
@Service
class Schedule {

    enum Repeat { NONE, WEEKLY, MONTHLY, MONTHLY_LAST_WEEKDAY }

    /** What is kept: the host's zone and the instants. No LocalDateTime is stored, because it means nothing alone. */
    record Webinar(long id, String title, ZoneId hostZone, int durationMinutes, List<Instant> sessions) {
    }

    record Session(Instant startsAt, OffsetDateTime hostTime, OffsetDateTime viewerTime, OffsetDateTime viewerEndTime, long viewerDayShift) {
    }

    record WebinarView(long id, String title, String hostZone, String viewerZone, int durationMinutes, List<Session> sessions) {
    }

    private final Clock clock;
    private final Map<Long, Webinar> webinars = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();   // shortcut: in memory, lost on restart; a real app uses a table
    private final AtomicLong ids = new AtomicLong();

    Schedule(Clock clock) {
        this.clock = clock;
    }

    WebinarView create(String title, LocalDateTime startsAt, ZoneId zone, ZoneOffset offset, int durationMinutes, Repeat repeat, int count) {
        if (repeat == Repeat.NONE && count != 1) {
            throw unprocessable("A one-off webinar has 1 session; use repeat MONTHLY or MONTHLY_LAST_WEEKDAY for " + count + ".");
        }
        DayOfWeek weekday = startsAt.getDayOfWeek();
        if (repeat == Repeat.MONTHLY_LAST_WEEKDAY && !startsAt.toLocalDate().equals(startsAt.toLocalDate().with(TemporalAdjusters.lastInMonth(weekday)))) {
            throw unprocessable(startsAt.toLocalDate() + " is not the last " + weekday + " of its month.");
        }
        List<Instant> sessions = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
            LocalDateTime local = switch (repeat) {
                // Always from the first date: Jan 31 + 1 month = Feb 28 (or 29), + 2 months = Mar 31. Chaining would stick at 28.
                case WEEKLY -> startsAt.plusWeeks(i);   // wall-clock weeks in the host's zone, not 7 x 24 hours
                case NONE, MONTHLY -> startsAt.plusMonths(i);
                case MONTHLY_LAST_WEEKDAY -> startsAt.plusMonths(i).with(TemporalAdjusters.lastInMonth(weekday));
            };
            sessions.add(resolve(local, zone, i == 0 ? offset : null));
        }
        if (!sessions.getFirst().isAfter(clock.instant())) {
            throw unprocessable("The first session, " + startsAt + " in " + zone + ", has already started.");
        }
        Webinar webinar = new Webinar(ids.incrementAndGet(), title, zone, durationMinutes, List.copyOf(sessions));
        webinars.put(webinar.id(), webinar);
        return view(webinar, zone);
    }

    Optional<WebinarView> find(long id, ZoneId viewerZone) {
        return Optional.ofNullable(webinars.get(id)).map(w -> view(w, viewerZone == null ? w.hostZone() : viewerZone));
    }

    /**
     * A wall-clock time in a zone is not always one instant: in a daylight saving gap it is none (clocks jump past
     * it), in an overlap it is two (clocks repeat it). Both are refused unless the client names the offset it means.
     */
    static Instant resolve(LocalDateTime local, ZoneId zone, ZoneOffset offset) {
        List<ZoneOffset> valid = zone.getRules().getValidOffsets(local);
        if (valid.isEmpty()) {
            throw unprocessable(local + " does not exist in " + zone + ": the clocks skip it for daylight saving.");
        }
        if (offset != null) {
            if (!valid.contains(offset)) {
                throw unprocessable(local + " in " + zone + " is at " + valid.getFirst() + ", not " + offset + ".");
            }
            return local.atOffset(offset).toInstant();
        }
        if (valid.size() > 1) {
            throw unprocessable(local + " happens twice in " + zone + " (" + valid.get(0) + " and " + valid.get(1)
                    + ") as the clocks go back; send \"offset\" to choose.");
        }
        return local.atOffset(valid.getFirst()).toInstant();
    }

    private static WebinarView view(Webinar w, ZoneId viewer) {
        List<Session> sessions = w.sessions().stream()
                .map(s -> new Session(s, s.atZone(w.hostZone()).toOffsetDateTime(), s.atZone(viewer).toOffsetDateTime(),
                        s.plus(Duration.ofMinutes(w.durationMinutes())).atZone(viewer).toOffsetDateTime(),
                        ChronoUnit.DAYS.between(s.atZone(w.hostZone()).toLocalDate(), s.atZone(viewer).toLocalDate()))).toList();
        return new WebinarView(w.id(), w.title(), w.hostZone().getId(), viewer.getId(), w.durationMinutes(), sessions);
    }

    static ErrorResponseException unprocessable(String detail) {
        ProblemDetail p = ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, detail);
        p.setTitle("Not a schedulable time");
        return new ErrorResponseException(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, p, null);
    }
}

Challenge 3 · design on paper, no code

When a country changes its clocks

A government announces, six months ahead, that it will stop daylight saving. Webinars in that zone are already stored as instants. Which ones are now wrong, how would you find them, and would storing the host's local time and zone (and computing the instant later) have been better for future events?

Implementation approach

  1. Write the trap test with both old versions.
  2. Decide what the client sends (wall-clock time and zone) and what the server keeps (moment and zone).
  3. Resolve every session on its own date; refuse gaps and overlaps unless the client is explicit.
  4. Inject a Clock, and pin it in tests.

Design alternatives and trade-offs

ApproachWhat it costsVerdict
Store Instant + host zone; resolve each session in the zoneZone rule changes after creation are not followed.Chosen
Store LocalDateTime onlyNo moment at all: wrong for everyone elsewhere.The trap
Store local time + zone; compute the instant on readFollows rule changes; every read recomputes, and sorting by moment needs care.Better for far-future events
Store OffsetDateTimeKeeps one offset; a series cannot follow daylight saving.For past events
Silently shift gap times (Java's default)02:30 becomes 03:30 without anyone choosing it.Surprising

Database design

None in this station. In PostgreSQL, a moment is a timestamptz column (stored as UTC), and the host's zone a text column holding the region id. A timestamp column without time zone is this station's trap in SQL form.

A Foundations station: the considerations to know, no runbook.

Time zone data changes
Governments change their rules several times a year somewhere. The JDK ships the IANA time zone database; keep the JDK updated, or use the tzupdater tool between releases.
Servers run in UTC
Never rely on the server's default zone. Ask for a zone explicitly everywhere, as this code does.
Show offsets
Times sent to clients carry their offset, so no client has to guess.
One clock
Code that asks the real clock directly cannot be tested at midnight, at month end or on 29 February. Inject a Clock.

Interview takeaways

Instant, LocalDateTime, ZonedDateTime, OffsetDateTime: when each?

Instant for a moment (storage, logs). LocalDateTime for a wall-clock reading with no place (what a user types). ZonedDateTime for a moment in a region with rules, for arithmetic across daylight saving. OffsetDateTime for a moment with a fixed offset, for sending over the wire.

What happens with 02:30 on a spring-forward night?

It does not exist. getValidOffsets returns nothing; ZonedDateTime.of would silently move it forward. Decide: refuse it, or move it on purpose.

Why not add 24 hours to get tomorrow at the same time?

On a daylight saving day, a day is 23 or 25 hours. Add a day to the local date-time, then resolve it in the zone.

How do you test code that depends on the current time?

Inject java.time.Clock and call LocalDate.now(clock) or clock.instant(). In tests, use Clock.fixed, here through Spring's @TestBean.

What is Jan 31 plus one month?

Feb 28 (29 in a leap year): plusMonths clamps to the month end. Always add from the original date for a series, or you get stuck on the 28th.
